# Psalm 94 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** O-God-of vengeance YHWH, O-God-of vengeance shine-forth!

**2** Rise-up O-Judge-of the-earth; return recompense upon the-proud.

**3** How-long the-wicked O-YHWH, how-long the-wicked will-exult?

**4** They-pour-out they-speak arrogance; boast-themselves all doers-of iniquity.

**5** Your-people O-YHWH they-crush, and-your-inheritance they-afflict.

**6** The-widow and-the-sojourner they-kill, and-the-fatherless they-murder.

**7** And-they-say, 'Not will-see Yah, and-not will-understand the-God-of Jacob.'

**8** Understand O-brutish among-the-people; and-fools when will-you-be-wise?

**9** The-planter-of the-ear will-he not hear? The-former-of the-eye will-he not see?

**10** The-discipliner-of nations will-he not rebuke? The-teacher-of man knowledge?

**11** YHWH knows the-thoughts-of man, that they-are breath.

**12** Blessed the-man whom you-discipline O-Yah, and-from-your-law you-teach-him,

**13** To-give-him-rest from-days-of evil, until is-dug for-the-wicked a-pit.

**14** For not will-abandon YHWH his-people, and-his-inheritance not he-will-forsake.

**15** For unto righteousness will-return judgment, and-after-it all the-upright-of heart.

**16** Who will-rise-up for-me against evildoers? Who will-stand-up for-me against doers-of iniquity?

**17** If-not YHWH a-help for-me, soon would-have-dwelt my-soul in-silence.

**18** When I-said, 'Has-slipped my-foot,' your-steadfast-love O-YHWH held-me-up.

**19** In-multitude-of my-anxious-thoughts within-me, your-consolations delight my-soul.

**20** Will-it-be-allied with-you a-throne-of destruction, framer-of mischief by-statute?

**21** They-band-together against the-soul-of the-righteous, and-blood innocent they-condemn.

**22** And-YHWH has-been to-me a-stronghold, and-my-God the-rock-of my-refuge.

**23** And-he-will-return upon-them their-iniquity, and-in-their-evil he-will-destroy-them; will-destroy-them YHWH our-God.

---
## EMET Literal Notes

- **94:9-10**: Classic a fortiori argument: the Creator of ears/eyes must himself hear/see — design implies capacity in the Designer.

- **94:19**: 'In-multitude-of my-anxious-thoughts... your-consolations delight my-soul' — one of the Psalter's most personal statements of divine comfort.

— EMET
